rules.title: Just Cause Required for Eviction Under Rent Ordinance
rules.requirement: A landlord must have one of 17 enumerated "just cause" reasons as the dominant motive to evict a tenant from a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance. The mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not by itself constitute just cause.

coverage_conditions.notes: Applies to rental units covered by the Rent Ordinance. Tenancies otherwise exempt from the Ordinance's rent-increase limitations — including units in buildings that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, units eligible for increases under the state Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act, and units with rent regulated by another government agency — remain subject to these just-cause eviction requirements.

rules.exemptions: Removal of certain housing services (e.g., garage/parking facilities, storage spaces, laundry rooms) also requires just cause, except a landlord complying with Ordinance Section 37.2(r) may temporarily remove parking and storage access to perform mandatory soft-story seismic retrofit work required by the Building Code.
rules.interaction: One of the 17 causes is withdrawal of all rental units from the market under the state Ellis Act; another references Costa-Hawkins-eligible tenancies as still covered by just-cause protections even though exempt from local rent-increase caps.
rules.penalty: A landlord who evicts or attempts to evict a tenant unlawfully may be subject to substantial civil and/or criminal liability.
rules.quoted_span: a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction. Note that the mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute "just cause"
